title: RegistryRecord
description: The part of a network registry record that BACP reads about one subscriber: its id, its BACP role, its signing keys and their validity, and, for a Mandate Manager or a PSP, the Trusted Surface origins, the notify endpoint, the numbers it calls from, the languages and the modalities it serves. For a human support operator it names the operator and the person. A registry may carry more fields, and a reader ignores any field it does not know. Whether a given registry, such as the ONDC network registry, can carry these fields is not settled.

subscriber_id.description: The registry subscriber id of the participant. For a Mandate Manager or a PSP it is the value that Presentation.surface carries.

bacp_role.description: The BACP role of the keys in this record: the registry role that Signature.role carries.

keys.description: The subscriber's public keys, each resolvable by its kid.

valid_until.description: When the record stops being valid. A reader MUST NOT use the record after it.

status.description: active while the record may be relied on, revoked once the registry has withdrawn it. A revocation takes effect at the next registry refresh, as for any other key.

operator_id.description: The agent operator that the keys serve. REQUIRED when bacp_role is support_operator.

person_ref.description: A pairwise pseudonymous reference to the one person who holds the key of a support operator, never an Aadhaar number. REQUIRED when bacp_role is support_operator, and every support operator key belongs to one person: there are no shared desk keys.

ts_origins.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: the web origins from which its Trusted Surface serves a step-up, as https origins only (scheme, host and optional port, no path, as in RFC 6454). The gateway mints trusted_surface_url, and accepts a Mandate Manager's mandate-approval link, only on an origin of the step-up's signer. A tel: number is never an origin.

ts_notify_url.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: the https endpoint to which the gateway sends a content-free push, a gateway-signed POST of {step_up_id, expires_at}, when no origin of the signer conforms. The Trusted Surface then fetches the render by step_up_id.

ts_call_numbers.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: E.164 numbers from which its Trusted Surface places calls. They are informative, a hint that an agent may speak and never an authenticator, and always carry the sentence that the bank never asks for a PIN on a call it makes.

ts_languages.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: the languages in which its Trusted Surface renders a step-up. Absence of a language means that the Trusted Surface does not claim it.

ts_modalities.description: For a Mandate Manager or a PSP: the modalities in which its Trusted Surface presents a step-up.
